purpose: Diltiazem is used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and certain irregular heart rhythms. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps lower your risk of having a heart attack or stroke. It can also help your heart beat more regularly and reduce episodes of chest pain.
how_it_works: Your heart and blood vessels use calcium to contract and tighten. Diltiazem blocks some of that calcium from entering the heart muscle and blood vessel walls. This causes your blood vessels to relax and widen, your heart to beat a little more slowly and with less force, which lowers your blood pressure and reduces the workload on your heart.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include swelling in your feet or ankles, dizziness, headache, flushing (feeling warm or red in the face), slow heartbeat, nausea, and feeling tired. These are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, heart failure, or very low blood pressure. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Let your doctor know all other medicines you take, especially heart or blood pressure medications, since interactions can be dangerous.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on what condition is being treated and whether you are taking a short-acting or long-acting (extended-release) form. A common starting dose for high blood pressure with the extended-release form is 120 to 240 mg once daily. Short-acting tablets are often taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor will find the dose that works best for you, so always follow their specific instructions.
